Breadth cracked back open after Wednesday's deceleration: NYSE/Nasdaq decliner ratios widened back out to roughly 4:1/3.55:1, new 52-week lows surged, and all but one S&P sector fell -- unambiguously broad, not narrow. No fresher weekly fund-flow cut has been found; the week-ended-11-Nov BofA/EPFR and Lipper prints are now carried forward for a third straight day and still predate the entire four-session 16-19 Nov selloff.

breadth.note: Breadth cracked back open on 19 Nov after Wednesday's brief deceleration: NYSE/Nasdaq decliner ratios widened back out to roughly 4-to-1 and 3.55-to-1 (from ~1.36-to-1/1.18-to-1 on 18 Nov), new 52-week lows surged (642 NYSE, 529 Nasdaq) against only a handful of new highs, and all but one S&P sector fell. This reads as an unambiguously broad, not narrow, risk-off -- the small-cap/breadth stabilization hinted at by Russell 2000's 18-Nov gain did not survive 19 Nov's reacceleration (Russell -2.18%), and the precious-metals miner-specific unwind seen on 18 Nov (GDX/SILJ far underperforming GLD/SLV) gave way to a more uniform decline across bullion, miners, equities and crypto alike on 19 Nov.

flows.narrative: No fresher weekly fund-flow print has been published since the week ended 11 Nov 2026 -- the same cut carried forward for a third consecutive day. BofA/EPFR's week-ended-11-Nov report logged global equity inflows of +$98.3bn (largest since June 2026), led by a sixth-straight-week +$63.6bn US inflow and a fifth-straight-week China inflow, alongside a -$17.9bn money-market outflow. Reuters/LSEG Lipper's broader fund universe instead flagged Europe as the week's single biggest draw (+$35.13bn, strongest since June 2021), with US equities +$6.6bn and EM equities +$4.65bn, plus a -$37.48bn money-market reversal; ICI's independently-sourced MMF series corroborates the cash-outflow direction (-$35.72bn for the week ended 11 Nov). None of this reflects the four-session 16-19 Nov selloff -- in particular Thursday 19 Nov's acceleration (S&P -2.02%, VIX +15.8%, gold/silver/miners and BTC all down again, in contrast to 18 Nov's narrower miner-specific unwind) is not captured in any confirmed weekly fund-flow cut. The next editions (overdue by this point) remain the key data point for whether this is a genuine flow reversal out of risk assets or a sentiment/price-only move that flows haven't caught up to yet.
